item.placement_note: New actual smooth separable Hilbert parameter-family/universal-section supplier, with exact fixed support and collar restriction; root integrates canonical metadata.
item.statement_excerpt:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix compact transverse strip data and a smooth background path $J_t^*$ as in the actual higher Sobolev strip-chart construction, with exact all-$t$ product generator neighborhoods. Assume $J_t^*$ is constant in $t$ on endpoint collars $[0,\eta]$ and $[1-\eta,1]$, where $0<\eta<1/2$. Let $P\subset[0,1]\times X$ be a closed protected set containing those collars and $[0,1]\times V$, where $V$ is an open neighborhood of all generators. The complement $O=([0,1]\times X)\setminus P$ is the free variation region. Spatial neighborhoods of divisors, a diagonal, or any further sets can also be included in $P$. If tameness is required, let $\omega$ be a smooth two-form on an open $W\subset X$, assume the spatial projection of $\overline O$ is a compact subset of $W$, and assume $J_t^*$ is $\omega$-tame on $W$.

There are a separable real Hilbert parameter space $H=\ell^2(\mathbb N;\mathbb R)$, a ball $B_H(0,r)$, and actual smooth paths $J_t(a)$ for $a$ in that ball, such that $J(0)=J^*$, $J(a)^2=-I$, and $J(a)=J^*$ on $P$. In particular every path is constant on the same actual endpoint collars and retains the exact generator charts and all protected values. The family preserves the stated tameness. For every integer $k\ge0$, $a\mapsto J(a)$ is smooth as a map into the global $C^k$ coefficient space, with compatible derivatives at all orders; every $J(a)$ is a smooth path.

At any parameter $a$, finite linear combinations of parameter tangent directions are $C^k$ dense in the smooth compactly supported fields $Y$ on $O$ satisfying $YJ(a)+J(a)Y=0$, for every finite $k$. Their evaluations span that entire anti-complex-linear fiber at each point of $O$. Thus, for each nonzero $v\in T_xX$ and $(t,x)\in O$, the map $b\mapsto(d_aJ[b])_t(x)v$ is onto $T_xX$.

On the actual higher Sobolev strip configuration manifold, this family defines a genuine smooth universal section
$$\mathcal F(a,u)=u_s+J_t(a,u)u_t$$
with the actual local-addition $H^3\cap\mathcal X^1\to H^2$ domain and bundle target. At a zero its derivative is the actual geometric expression
$$d\mathcal F_{(a,u)}(b,\xi)=P_{a,u}\xi+(d_aJ[b])_t(u)u_t,$$
and it has closed range. At any zero where this derivative is onto, the actual universal zero set is locally a separable Hilbert manifold, and its projection to the parameter ball is Fredholm of real index $\operatorname{ind}P_{a,u}$. At such a zero the derivative of that projection is onto if and only if the actual fixed-parameter strip operator $P_{a,u}$ is onto.

This supplies the actual fixed-support parameter family and universal setup. It does not assert that every nonconstant strip has a suitable injective point in $O$, that the universal derivative is onto at every zero, or that a generic parameter has the original global regularity conclusions. In particular interior injective-point density alone does not establish the required availability outside a fixed endpoint collar.

proof_step_donor_fragments.exact_current_text: Construct a countable collection $B_n$ of smooth endomorphism fields compactly supported in $O$, anti-commuting with $J^*$, whose finite span is dense in every finite $C^k$ norm on smooth compactly supported such fields. Fix a finite smooth coordinate atlas on $X$ and its induced local tangent frames, and rational product-coordinate balls with compact closure inside $O$ and one such atlas chart. In each ball take the fixed smooth bump $\varphi((z-q)/r)$, for rational center $q$ and positive rational radius $r$, times each real matrix unit of the local frame; extend by zero and apply the smooth fiber projection $A\mapsto(A+J^*AJ^*)/2$. These are countably many fields and anti-commute with $J^*$. To verify density, split any given compactly supported field by a finite smooth partition subordinate to such relatively compact charts; an ordinary finite partition follows by finitely many bumps positive on its compact support and dividing their sum. Its local coefficient functions extend smoothly by zero. Convolution with the normalized bump at rational radii tending to zero converges with every prescribed finite number of derivatives, because differentiation commutes with convolution and the derivatives are uniformly continuous on a compact support. Each convolution integral is approximated in $C^k$ by finite Riemann sums with rational centers: uniform continuity of the derivatives of the translated bump gives convergence of the same finite sums for all derivatives through order $k$. Approximate the finitely many coefficients by rational numbers if desired. The supports remain in the chosen chart and $O$ when the radius and the grid are small enough. The resulting finite combinations of the enumerated matrix bumps approximate the local field, and the smooth projection preserves convergence and fixes the original anti-commuting field. Summing the finite partition proves the assertion. At any $p\in O$, a rational ball containing $p$ with positive bump value supplies all projected matrix units there, so their evaluations span the full anti-$J^*(p)$ fiber. Zero or repeated entries may be included to obtain one sequence indexed by $\mathbb N$. [given, construct, algebra]

Fix global coefficient $C^k$ norms using the finite atlas on the compact manifold $[0,1]\times X$. Put $$c_n=\frac{2^{-n}}{1+\max_{0\le j\le n}\|B_n\|_{C^j}},\qquad B(a)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nc_nB_n.$$ For each fixed $k$, $\sum_n c_n^2\|B_n\|_{C^k}^2<\infty$: its tail $n\ge k$ is bounded by $\sum_n4^{-n}$ and its preceding terms are finite. Cauchy–Schwarz therefore gives convergence of every derivative through order $k$, uniformly, with norm at most $C_k\|a\|_{\ell^2}$. The compatible uniform derivative limits are the derivatives of the limiting field, by the coordinate fundamental theorem applied successively. Thus $B(a)$ is smooth, anti-commutes with $J^*$, and defines a bounded linear map $H\to C^k$ for every $k$. Every term vanishes on $P$, hence so does the limit. Derivatives vanish there as well, though equality of values suffices. In particular the sum vanishes on the same fixed endpoint collars; this is stronger than merely summing bumps each with its own possibly shrinking collar. The positive constants $c_n$ leave the finite span and all pointwise spanning conclusions unchanged. Separability and completeness of the real sequence Hilbert space follow from truncation to finitely many coordinates with rational entries and the coordinatewise limit of any Cauchy sequence, whose squared tail bounds pass to the limit. [step 1.1, construct, algebra]

Choose $r>0$ so $\|B(a)\|_{C^0}<1/2$ for $\|a\|<r$, and define $$J(a)=J^*(I+B(a))(I-B(a))^{-1}.$$ The inverse is its uniformly convergent geometric series. Anti-commutation gives $(I-B)J^*=J^*(I+B)$, hence direct multiplication shows $J(a)^2=-I$. It equals $J^*$ on $P$. Matrix inversion is smooth in each $C^k$ coefficient algebra: products obey the finite Leibniz estimate, the inverse has bounded derivatives by differentiating $(I-B)R=I$, and locally its inverse is the convergent Neumann series around any invertible coefficient field. The difference identity for two inverses gives derivative $R\,dB\,R$, with a quadratic remainder, and repeated differentiation proves all higher norm derivatives. Combining with step 2.1 proves the stated compatible smooth maps $H\to C^k$. For tameness, on the compact spatial projection of $\overline O$ the continuous positive function $\omega_x(v,J_t^*v)$ on unit tangent vectors has a positive minimum $\kappa$. The finite metric and coefficient bounds give $\|J(a)-J^*\|_{C^0}\le C\|B(a)\|_{C^0}$. Shrink $r$ so $|\omega(v,(J(a)-J^*)v)|\le\kappa|v|^2/2$ there. Tameness follows on this compact set and is unchanged elsewhere, since outside $O$ the variation is zero. No symplectic closedness of $\omega$ is needed for this pointwise claim. [step 2.1, construct, algebra]

The tangent-density assertion holds at every parameter, not only at zero. Write $B=B(a)$ and $R=(I-B)^{-1}$. Differentiation gives $$dJ[C]=2J^*RCR.$$ This is a linear isomorphism from the anti-$J^*$ fiber to the anti-$J(a)$ fiber. One can verify invertibility either directly with inverse $C=-\tfrac12(I-B)J^*Y(I-B)$ or by differentiating the inverse coordinate formula $B=(A-I)(A+I)^{-1}$, where $A=-J^*J$. These formulas are defined in the same norm neighborhood and preserve the anti-commuting identities by multiplication. They also give bounded smooth coefficient isomorphisms in each finite $C^k$ norm and preserve compact support. Thus step 1.1 applied to the inverse image of a compactly supported $Y$ proves tangent density, and its pointwise spanning assertion proves fiber surjectivity. Finally for a nonzero $v$, any prescribed $w$ is $Yv$ for some anti-$J(a)$ endomorphism: on the real plane spanned by $v,J(a)v$ prescribe $Yv=w$, $YJ(a)v=-J(a)w$, and set $Y=0$ on its $J(a)$-invariant orthogonal complement for the invariant metric $g+g(J(a)\cdot,J(a)\cdot)$. The plane is two-dimensional because $J(a)^2=-I$. Consequently parameter evaluation on $v$ is onto, with a finite-support parameter vector for each such prescribed value. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

The configuration and range bundle of [F1] can be used for every parameter, with the same local addition. The boundary structures and exact generator charts are fixed since $P$ contains the endpoint collars and $[0,1]\times V$. In a chart at a smooth constant-end reference $u_0$, the expression is $$\mathcal F(a,\xi)=\mathcal T_\xi\bigl(\partial_s\mathcal E(u_0,\xi)+J_t(a,\mathcal E(u_0,\xi))\partial_t\mathcal E(u_0,\xi)\bigr).$$ Every mixed parameter and spatial coefficient derivative has a locally bounded $C^k$ norm by step 3.1. The actual $H^2$ algebra, $H^3\subset C^1$, Taylor remainders and weak chain rules in [F1] therefore prove joint smoothness $H\times(H^3\cap\mathcal X^1)\to H^2$, by the same finite product estimates, now with parameter variations as additional bounded coefficient factors. On the ends a small configuration chart remains within $V$, where parameter variations vanish identically, and the reference is constant. Thus no nonintegrable constant offset is inserted on the infinite strip. The range trivializations are precisely those of [F1]. Zeros are actual smooth finite-energy solutions by that result, since for each parameter the exact ends and fixed boundary structures are retained. Differentiation at a zero gives exactly the asserted $P_{a,u}\xi+(d_aJ[b])u_t$; derivative of the range trivialization multiplies the zero section and contributes nothing. [F1, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

At a zero write $E=H^3\cap\mathcal X^1$, $Y=H^2$, $P_0=P_{a,u}$ and $K:H\to Y$ for the bounded parameter derivative. The actual $P_0$ is Fredholm by [F1] and [F2]. Let $C=Y/\operatorname{Ran}P_0$, a finite-dimensional quotient, and $q:Y\to C$ its quotient map. The universal derivative has range $q^{-1}(\operatorname{im}(qK))$, closed because every subspace of the finite-dimensional $C$ is closed. If it is onto, choose finitely many parameter vectors whose $qK$ images form a basis of $C$; this is finite choice. They give a bounded linear right inverse $j:C\to H$ to $qK$. The fixed operator $P_0$ has a bounded inverse on an $H^1$ kernel complement to its closed range by [F2], and its restriction maps $H^2\cap\operatorname{Ran}P_0$ boundedly to $H^3$ by the higher estimate there. Denote this range inverse by $Q_0$. Then $$f\longmapsto\bigl(jqf,\ Q_0(f-Kjqf)\bigr)$$ is a specified bounded right inverse of the actual universal derivative. Apply [F3] to get its actual local separable Hilbert zero chart. Its tangent space is $\{(b,\xi):P_0\xi+Kb=0\}$. Projection to $H$ has kernel $\ker P_0$ and image $\ker(qK)$, so its cokernel is isomorphic to $C$ because $qK$ is onto. It is Fredholm with index $\dim\ker P_0-\dim C=\operatorname{ind}P_0$. That projection derivative is onto exactly when $C=0$, which is equivalent to $P_0$ onto. Countable local charts follow from the second-countable product in [F1] and the separable parameter space, using Countable Choice if a chart subcover is selected. No claim that the displayed right inverse exists when the universal derivative is not onto has been made. [F1, F2, F3, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

All analytic constructions are actual smooth fields, convergent Hilbert series, explicit local section formulas and specified finite-dimensional lifts. What remains for universal transversality is the substantive assertion that the universal derivative is onto at the desired zeros. The pointwise spanning result of step 4.1 only applies at $(t,u(s,t))\in O$; it cannot supply a variation at a protected point or at an entire fixed endpoint collar. In particular countably many unrestricted interior bump supports cannot replace this construction while retaining an actual common endpoint collar. Proving that each relevant strip has an available injective point, or proving regularity by a separate argument when none is available, remains necessary. These limitations do not alter any of the actual family, density or universal local-setup conclusions just proved. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, construct] ∎
